summary: This video presents a comprehensive landscape post-processing workflow focused on a high-detail fall-color scene. Beginning with a six-frame focus stack to achieve sharp foreground and background details, the presenter flattens dynamic range for consistent light and then uses Photoshop and Camera Raw to color-grade by zones. The core creative technique centers on separating mountains and creating depth through a blend of clone-paint and Orton-style glow, followed by targeted, history-based adjustments (including Selective Color, calibration, and sponge/dodge/burn) to shape light, color, and atmosphere. The workflow emphasizes precise brushwork, multi-layer separation, and atmospheric haze to guide the viewer toward the light while preserving intricate foreground and midground detail, culminating in a cohesive, three-dimensional landscape image.

sections.title: Focus stacking setup and dynamic-range flattening
sections.description: The speaker identifies the goal of the stack (accentuate mid-ground colors and left-biased light) and explains that initial DR expansion is necessary to retain sky and shadow detail before heavy color work.

sections.title: Loading, aligning, and blending stacked frames in Photoshop
sections.description: Six images are opened in Photoshop, loaded into a stack, auto-aligned to compensate slight focal-length shifts, and then auto-blended to combine the stack with seamless tones. The presenter notes potential memory issues and compares Photoshop with Helicon for alignment.

sections.title: Zone-based color adjustments in Camera Raw and selective color basics
sections.description: After flattening the stack, the image is opened in Camera Raw. The presenter uses calibration controls (luminosity/saturation) to intensify foliage color, then introduces selective color/HSL concepts to control blue and red regions while preserving other zones.

sections.title: History Select workflow and selective sky recall
sections.description: The technique centers on history-based selective application to apply, erase, and blend prior adjustments. The host demonstrates painting adjustments into the sky separately from the rest of the image and re-applying steps with controlled opacity to avoid obvious composites.

sections.title: Light painting and atmospheric separation using clone-paint and Orton-style glow
sections.description: A multiphase sequence shows duplicating the image, applying Orton-style blur and glow on a background layer, then using the clone stamp with a hard brush to paint from the blurred layer into the sharp foreground, creating pronounced depth and three-dimensional separation of ridges. The process includes precise edge erasing with soft brushes and iterative layering to simulate atmospheric haze and light diffusion.

sections.title: Final refinements: luminosity, sky blues, and micro-adjustments
sections.description: The final pass emphasizes localized luminosity and color tuning, including blue calibration of skies, selective brightening of foreground light, sponge tool treatments for foliage saturation, and subtle dodging/burning for highlight emphasis. The section also covers minor crop/warp decisions and final quality checks.
